text:
lina: FYI incoming ticket from Brightline — their dedicated cluster ded-nyc-3 spiking 503s and token latency after a big long-context job. They say it started ~20:05 UTC and correlates w/ a dataset import. logs attached in ticket.

jordan: Can you paste the snippet of the error and the time window? 503s usually mean backend throttles / eviction pressure.

lina: Sure — root message from customer: "requests started 20:04:32 UTC, steady 500-30% of calls 503 or 504, CPU/GPU fine, but token generation pauses ~1.5-3s then 429/503. Not seeing model OOM."

mikaela: Pasted a quick grep of the runtime logs for ded-nyc-3 20:00-20:10: 
```
[20:04:33] eviction: tenant=brightline ctx_len=16384 evict_count=1172
[20:04:33] kv_alloc: node=ded-nyc-3 used=92% free=8% frag_ratio=0.46
[20:04:34] throttle: tenant=brightline reason=kv_pressure action=reject
[20:04:35] autoscale: decision=defer reason=cooldown windows=300s
[20:04:36] rpc: worker=wl-12 latency=2000ms status=503
```

sam: evac numbers look ugly. frag_ratio 0.46 is high — fragmentation causing fewer usable slabs, so eviction churn is high and autoscaler deferred because of cooldown. That would explain repeated throttles.

lina: Customer says they have a few very long-context batch jobs (16k tokens) and a burst of many small requests. Sounds like heavy KV churn + hot keys.

jordan: Can we get the KV metrics heatmap + slab allocation per tenant for that host? Also what was the autoscale policy (min/max/growth) for ded-nyc-3 at that time?

ops-bot: [autoscale-policy] ded-nyc-3: min_replicas=2 max_replicas=6 growth_rate=1.0 cooldown=300s current_replicas=3

mikaela: I pulled slab allocations (tenant-scope) — brightline had ~58% of active slabs but only 12% of total tokens in last hour. Hotkey pattern: a handful of contexts being rehoused repeatedly.

ayden: (joining) quick idea: if slab fragmentation + high eviction -> reactive autoscaler cooldown prevents scale out in time. Possible mitigations: bump ded capacity (manual), reduce per-tenant max_context, or enable pre-warm for long-context job.

jordan: Agreed. Short-term: can we temporarily increase dedicated pool by 1 replica to relieve pressure while we debug? Who can approve?

lina: I'll request a manual scale with infra (need approval). Also asked customer to pause the import job for 30m to let cache stabilize.

support-qa: Repro note I started locally with a tenant running mixed loads: one steady 16k context stream + many small requests. Observed eviction churn and >30% operation rejects within ~3m. I saved a minimal repro script and heap trace.

mikaela: Can you drop the repro script in the thread? Also enable kv_debug=1 for that tenant so we get per-op eviction traces next time.

support-qa: Put it in GH gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/support-repro-216000 — includes load generator (python), config changes and expected metrics.

jordan: Thanks. Next steps: 1) Manual scale + notify Brightline, 2) run repro w/ kv_debug to capture eviction timeline, 3) run heap profiler on ded-nyc-3 to inspect fragmentation, 4) evaluate autoscale cooldown tuning (reduce from 300s for heavy long-context tenants) and 5) consider per-tenant caching isolation (QA spike).

lina: Opened SR-4532 and tagged eng-runtime + eng-sre. Assigned jordan to lead investigation.  Brightline agreed to pause import for 45m.

sam: While we investigate, quick mitigation we applied: per-tenant eviction threshold lowered for brightline and we enabled prefix caching for frequent contexts. Reduced immediate evict_count by ~70% in test.

jordan: Good. Also filing a follow-up to look at slab allocator improvements (coalescing free regions) — fragmentation is the smoking gun.

mikaela: Added logs from the scale operation: 
```
[20:06:12] scale: manual request +1 replica -> accepted
[20:06:45] node-registration: wl-17 joined pool
[20:07:12] cache-rebalance: start -> moved 210 contexts off wl-12
[20:08:00] kv_alloc: used=67% frag_ratio=0.22
[20:08:10] throttle: tenant=brightline action=lift
```

lina: Customer confirmed errors dropped to baseline after 20:09. They're asking for long-term fix and SLA notes.

jordan: We'll propose: (A) autoscale policy change for clusters that serve known long-context tenants (lower cooldown OR faster growth), (B) per-tenant cache reservations for heavy tenants, (C) allocator defragmentation work. I'll draft a runbook.

support-qa: QA will run the repro nightly and send eval metrics to the console alerts.

mikaela: Marking this resolved for now; moving to backlog epic INF-821 (slab-defrag) for eng-runtime. :white_check_mark:

lina: Thanks team. I'll keep SR-4532 open until we have the runbook and either code or policy changes.

jordan: Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
